transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Avery Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood Impl), Maya Patel (Praxis Head Eng), Carlos Ruiz (Praxis CTO), Ellen Park (Clinical Data), Diego Morales (Praxis DevOps)
Shared items: Kickoff deck (https://redwood.ai/implementation/kickoff-deck), onboarding runbook, security packet (link coming)

Summary (auto):
Short intro to rollout plan, confirm success criteria, discuss network and security requirements, agree next steps for pilot and technical deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, I'm the customer success manager and I'll run the kickoff. Um, short agenda - intros, success criteria, timeline, technical requirements, and next steps.
[00:22] Maya: Thanks, Jordan. Hi all, Maya here. We're excited to get started. Quick context, Praxis is building an in-product clinical triage assistant, we expect about 2k to 10k requests per day in month one and want to hit 50ms p50 for short chat turn, um, ideally.
[00:40] Carlos: Carlos here, CTO. Our constraints are data privacy for PHI-ish content, HIPAA-ish, so we need a private deployment or VPC with strong encryption and audit logs.
[00:56] Jordan: Totally heard that. We'll walk through Private and Dedicated options. Avery, do you want to start on architecture?
[01:02] Avery: Sure. Yeah so hi, Avery. On the Redwood side we have three paths: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC / on-prem). Given PHI concerns, most folks in regulated spaces choose Private with customer-managed networking and optional on-prem, or Dedicated with dedicated GPU pools plus contracted data handling.
[01:30] Ellen: If I can jump in, for clinical notes we can't send raw identifiable data to hosted endpoints. We need KMS integration and proof of encryption at rest.
[01:40] Samir: Absolutely. For Private we support KMS/HSM integrations, full audit logs, and you can bring your own key. We'll note the exact compliance docs.
[01:49] Diego: On networking, we use AWS VPC, we run EKS, and we'll need a list of IP ranges for allowlisting and some terraform examples. Also, how does the KV cache work - do you require persistent storage in our VPC?
[02:04] Avery: Good q. KV cache is ephemeral per serving node, we can configure shared cache in VPC if you want warm starts across instances. I'll send a doc with caching modes. For allowlist, we have static egress IPs for dedicated/private peering, Samir will prepare that.
[02:22] Jordan: Let's capture success criteria - Maya, what does "success" look like for Praxis in 6 weeks?
[02:30] Maya: Pilot needs to demonstrate 1) integration with our pipeline and SSO, 2) latency p50 under 150ms for 99% of sample prompt types, 3) redaction + PII detection working end-to-end, and 4) cost projection within our budget envelope.
[02:48] Jordan: Great, that's specific. We'll add those to the onboarding plan.
[02:55] Carlos: On timelines - we have a compliance review on 2027-12-20, so ideally we want a working pilot before then. Is that realistic?
[03:03] Samir: Yes, if we get the sample data and access by 12-15, we can spin up a Private trial environment in 5-7 days and run the initial benchmarks. 12-20 is tight but achievable.
[03:12] Diego: Awesome. Network peering takes sometimes our security team's review though - can you provide a template for the security questionnaire?
[03:20] Jordan: We'll attach the standard security packet and a completed sample. Also we'll provide the SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[03:27] Ellen: On output quality - we need to run our standard eval set to ensure the model doesn't hallucinate clinical advice and that the reranking does safe-fallbacks. Does Redwood support eval hooks?
[03:38] Avery: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes evaluation harnesses and you can upload prompt/response sets. We also ship model recommendations and quantization suggestions for cost/perf. For safety, we'll help set up guardrails and a fallback to a smaller model or canned response on high-regret prompts.
[03:56] Carlos: Do you have references of other healthcare customers? We prefer customers who have completed HIPAA onboarding.
[04:02] Jordan: I can share anonymized references and a case study.
[04:06] Maya: On auth - we prefer SAML SSO. How long to get SSO integrated?
[04:12] Samir: Typically 3-5 business days once we have SAML metadata and a test user, then we can test and roll to your org.
[04:19] Diego: About routing - we have multi-region users, can Redwood route requests to nearest region to reduce latency?
[04:26] Avery: Yes, smart routing by region is supported. For Private deployments, we can set up regional endpoints or leverage our edge to route into your VPC. We'll document tradeoffs.
[04:39] Jordan: Okay, let's go through immediate deliverables. Jordan readout: we'll send SOW and pricing sheet; Avery will prepare network allowlist and terraform snippets; Samir will prepare KMS integration guide and SOC2 pack; Praxis provides sample dataset and traffic profile.
[04:58] Maya: Quick question on billing and usage: if we start on Dedicated and later move to Private, is migration supported without major changes?
[05:08] Jordan: Yes — the API and config layer is consistent, so you can pivot deployments. There are cost and data-control tradeoffs but we facilitate model/version pinning and rollouts.
[05:20] Carlos: Any blockers we should call out now?
[05:23] Diego: Our security team requires audit logs forwarded to their SIEM — is that supported?
[05:28] Samir: We can ship audit logs and integrate with common SIEMs; for Private you get raw logs, and for Dedicated we expose audit streams. We'll include a sample log schema.
[05:39] Ellen: For the pilot we'll need to set thresholds on hallucination and a list of examples that must pass.
[05:44] Avery: We'll work with you to codify those into the eval jobs.
[05:47] Jordan: Anything else before we wrap?
[05:50] Maya: Not on my side. Thanks. Just to confirm dates: SOW by 12-10, sample data 12-15, technical deep dive week of 12-20.
[05:59] Jordan: Yep. We'll also ask to schedule a security review meeting with our security eng next week.
[06:04] Carlos: Sounds good.
[06:06] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and checklist.

End of transcript.

Notes on quality: transcription contains the usual filler words and occasional mis-attribution; some technical terms may be slightly off (e.g., KV cache spelled as "K V"), but overall capture is sufficient for onboarding planning.
